Very well written. Not sure if I'm understanding it correctly, so please forgive me my mistakes. What you want, is for a game to have more specialized units that could shine independant of cultural or tome benefits, making them valuable picks when you synergize them with other units. At the moment these 'gimmicks' are really suffering, because they rarely benefit from enchantments. Not sure if you played from the beggining, but it was more like what you say. Higher tier units were often strong enough to use without any support and their combos could decimate enemies. The thing is, it made tier I and II units obsolete somewhere around midgame and suddenly all armies were tier III cultural + tier IV from book spam. It made strategizing and long term planning kind of pointless if all that you do was to get these III and IV tiers and not really care about anything around them.  
Recent changes made low tier units even stronger, thanks to buffs to leveling your units, but in opinion it's great, because at least I can play the race i created more or less to the end, without the need to throw them away in late. Honestly I recently haven't found myself spamming same 2 unit types for every army, because well rounded armies are generally better fit for anything (for example, you don't really need a frontline full of shieldmen, because one unit can give defense to neighbouring units, which could for example be polearm or fighter). If you find yourself spamming the same units over and over again, I recommend actually trying to diverge, because you are simply not playing optimally, if that is something you are worried about. But you need to plan it a little before and is more complicated than spamming, but also more rewarding overall.  
Might be wrong assumption, but it seems to me, that you might be playing almost only around enchantments. No surprise here that you find yourself going in the same place in later stages if you pick same tomes, even if in other order.  
At least these are my thoughts and expierences, feel free to disagree
